title: AC-17.10 widened a design constraint's subject without widening its reason, so the register and tui-design.md disagree about whether a second realiser is a Highlander defect
body:
**`AC-17.10` WIDENED THE SUBJECT OF A DESIGN CONSTRAINT WITHOUT WIDENING ITS REASON, AND THE TWO NOW DISAGREE ON THE RECORD.**

`tui-design.md` §7, "Prose fields -- the external editor", binding constraint 2:

> **Reuse the existing resolver and the realise-then-open path.** `$VISUAL`-before-`$EDITOR` is already resolved once in the CLI; **a second resolver is the Highlander defect** in the one place this estate can least afford it.

`AC-17.10`, deriving from it:

> ... and the existing realise-then-open path -- **a second resolver or a second realiser is the Highlander defect** in the one place this estate can least afford it, **since `$VISUAL`-before-`$EDITOR` is already resolved once inside that same function.**

**THE `since` CLAUSE JUSTIFIES THE RESOLVER AND ONLY THE RESOLVER.** The criterion kept the design's reason verbatim and added `or a second realiser` to its subject. Nothing in either document says why a second REALISER would be a Highlander defect, and the reason offered cannot be stretched to cover it: a realiser does not resolve `$VISUAL`.

**WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A WORDING NIT.** It cost a node a build and a ruling. ic built `AC-17.10` correctly, then could not green `AT-17.10` because the realiser half appeared to demand reuse of `facade.edit` -- which **cannot take a field by construction**: it appends `.md`, decides by `Project::edit_disposition` on the FILENAME, calls `hydrate`, and refuses generated views. The row was ruled satisfied by vc on 2026-08-30 on three legs, one of which is this divergence. **A criterion strengthened past its source produces exactly this: an obligation that reads as binding, cannot be discharged, and has no author to ask.**

**THIS IS THE DOCUMENT-SCALE FORM OF THE RULE THE CONSTRAINT IS ABOUT.** Two homes for one constraint, holding two values. `intent/restart.md` names the class at document scale already; this is an instance inside the acceptance register, where it is worse, because a criterion is a gate and a design paragraph is not.

**THE RESIDUAL THE CLAUSE LEGITIMATELY POINTS AT IS FORWARD, NOT BACKWARD.** `tui::edit::Files::scratch` is now the one home for realising a field to a file. `AC-17.4`'s in-place prose, or the web face, growing its own scratch writer WOULD be the defect the widened clause names. So the fix is not to delete the realiser half -- it is to give it the reason it never had, or to move it to a criterion that owns that concern.

**NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY.** Editing `AC-17.10` while it is being closed is the class cc named as: a finding that argues its way into the row you are closing is a real defect laundered through a green. The reword belongs to whoever holds WP-17 after `AT-17.10` lands, or to hv.

**REPORTED BY:** vc, 2026-08-30, while ruling ic's clause-2 question.
